**Triage: `pm:queue` + `domain:engine-core`.** No release-board label — see below.

## Domain anchoring

`classifyError` is `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts:849`, with its three call sites at `:176`, `:892`, `:953` in the same file. `packages/formula` (CEL / `matches-filter` / RLS predicate evaluation) ⇒ **`domain:engine-core`**, same lane as its predecessor #6133 (`pm:dispatched`, `domain:engine-core`). Routed by landing site; the topic ("error classification / author-facing diagnostics") would have suggested `services` or `cli`, and neither is where the function lives.

## Stale-premise check — `origin/main` `72847c5`

The premise is *sharper* than filed, not staler. `cel-engine.ts:817` now carries the comment PR #6202 left behind:

> Why the class and not the message (#6133): `classifyError` used to decide …

— i.e. the file itself documents that reading the message was the root cause, and the fix was applied to exactly one branch. #6133 is **closed completed**, so the "parse branch fixed, `type` / `runtime` branches unchanged" split the body describes is the current state of main, and the restriction was deliberate (PR #6202's own reasoning: cel-js's `TypeChecker` picks error classes by phase, so structuring the rest needs its own pricing).

## Why `pm:queue` rather than `finding`

The body is an out-of-scope finding by origin, but it does not read as observation-class: it names the function and line, gives a four-line reproduction that a dev can paste, and the harm is concrete and inverted — a syntactically valid expression that fails at evaluation is reported to the author as `kind: 'parse'`, i.e. *"your expression is malformed"*, sending them to inspect a correct expression. `parse_status` / `syntax_mode` are ordinary field names, and `type` (the second affected branch) is a very common one.

Two things make this cheap to price, which is the other half of why it is queueable rather than held: PR #6202 already **measured** the target surface — 18 cel-js evaluation codes, of which the current keyword table classifies 17 correctly, with `unknown_variable` the single case that must stay in `type` (`lib/type-checker.js:16`, `isEvaluating ? evaluationError : typeError`). So the by-code table the body suggests has a known size and a known exception list, not an open-ended audit.

**PM mechanism assumption (verify, falsifying it is welcome):** that the by-code mapping can replace the keyword table outright, so that no branch of `classifyError` reads author-controlled text. The body's own claim is narrower — it does not assert "must fully structure". Measure before committing to the full removal; a partial route that fixes the two message-reading branches while keeping a smaller table is an acceptable outcome if the measurement says so.

## Not on the release board

The predecessor #6133 carried no `target:*` either. This is a wrong-diagnostic defect on an author-facing field: no data is lost, no contract is violated on the wire, nothing fails closed or open. It costs the author time, which is real, but it is not "the RC cannot ship" under any of the four blocking criteria. If a lane disagrees, the board is one label away.

## Dedup (three repos, open issues **and** PRs)

⚠️ The GitHub search API is not reachable from this seat (`/search/issues` answers *"sessions are bound to their configured repositories"*, returning a structurally empty result rather than an error). Dedup was done by paginating **all 442 open issues and PRs** across the three repos and matching locally on `classifyError`, `cel-engine`, `kind: 'parse'`, `EvaluationError`.

No open shadow. #6133 is closed (the fixed branch), and **#6132** (`cel-to-filter`'s separate `reason: 'parse-error'` keyword table) is the third entrance the body names — related, distinct landing site, deliberately left as its own item.

**ACCEPT (engine-core seat #6019, session `session_01MwoubC3jL271FYt9rGXwxb`; direct-acceptance path — the dev agent was killed by the account token limit while polling CI, so the PR body is the report of record).** PR #6677 reviewed against the diff and fresh CI: classifier now reads only structured contract (error class + code), the keyword table is deleted outright, and no branch reads text an author — or, sharper, a **row** — can write. Scope discipline held: `cel-to-filter.ts` / `getParseEnv` untouched (frozen pending #6132).

The PM mechanism assumption ("by-code can replace the table outright — measure") was answered decisively in the strong direction: (1) the residual arm was live and readable from **data** (`matches(record.name, record.re)` let a row value pick the error kind); (2) a `TypeError` arm would have been dead code (cel-js's checker throws it only inside `Environment#check`, which catches it). Six codes re-graded `type→runtime`, each shown to have been on `type` only because cel-js's prose contains the word; `no_matching_overload` deliberately unchanged with rationale in source. Reverse verification 9 red / 40 green with one honestly-reported prediction deviation (the underscored field-name case was already right — reported as a pin, not claimed as a catch). Out-of-scope finding filed as #6679 before the session died.

CI: 24/24 concluded green (ESLint + TypeScript Type Check both `success`), changeset present. Now: ready + auto-merge via the queue; issue closes on merge.
